kept.claim: The migration indexes [0] into the embed_category query result unconditionally; when no embed_category row exists in site_settings (fresh installs, or any site that never changed the default) the result is empty and PG::Result#[] raises IndexError, aborting the migration.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Migration crashes when `embed_category` has no matching row in `site_settings`

**Severity:** HIGH -- `rake db:migrate` aborts on fresh installs and on every site that never customised `embed_category`.

### The Problem

```ruby
category_id = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c
                    INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name
                    WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i
```

Site settings only get a row in `site_settings` when they are changed from their default. `embed_category` defaulted to `''` in `config/site_settings.yml`, so most sites have no row, and the INNER JOIN also yields nothing if the stored name no longer matches a category. The result set then has zero tuples and `[0]` is called on it anyway.

### Theory / Proof

`PG::Result#[](n)` raises `IndexError: Index 0 is out of range` when `n >= ntuples` (pg gem, `pgresult_aref`). It does not return `nil`, so the `.to_i` / `== 0` fallback on line 14 is never reached. The code even shows it knows about empty results -- line 19 checks `cmd_tuples > 0` for `embeddable_hosts` -- but the two earlier queries skip that guard.

### What happens today vs. what will break

It works only on a database where an admin once set `embed_category` to the exact name of an existing category. Every other install (including CI and `db:create db:migrate` on a new site) fails at this migration and blocks all later ones.

### Research

Other Discourse data migrations that read `site_settings` guard with `first` / `cmd_tuples` or use `SELECT ... LIMIT 1` and check for `nil` before indexing.

### Recommendation

```ruby
result = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c
                  INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name
                  WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")
category_id = result.ntuples > 0 ? result[0]['id'].to_i : 0

if category_id == 0
  result = execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")
  category_id = result.ntuples > 0 ? result[0]['value'].to_i : 0
end
```

(The `uncategorized_category_id` row is created by migration `20131022045114`, so the second query is safe in practice, but the same guard costs nothing.)
kept.evidence: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:9-11 indexes [0] on a result that can be empty. site_settings only gets a row when a setting is changed from its default, and embed_category defaulted to ''. The locked pg 0.18.1 (Gemfile.lock:220) raises IndexError from PG::Result#[] when the index is >= ntuples, so the fallback on line 14 is never reached. Line 19 guards the embeddable_hosts query with cmd_tuples but these queries have no guard. Correction: the uncategorized_category_id row is created by migration 20131022045114, so the line-15 query is safe.

kept.claim: The migration inserts raw embeddable_hosts lines (e.g. 'http://eviltrout.com', 'https://example.com/1234', CRLF or blank lines) without the normalisation that EmbeddableHost's before_validation applies, so record_for_host's lower(host) = 'eviltrout.com' lookup never matches and embedding breaks for upgraded sites; values are also string-interpolated into SQL without quoting.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Migrated hosts are not normalised, so existing `http://`-prefixed hosts stop matching after upgrade

**Severity:** HIGH -- sites that stored hosts with a scheme or path lose comment embedding silently after upgrading.

### The Problem

```ruby
records.each do |h|
  execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"
end
```

The raw line from the old setting is written as-is. The new lookup in `app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17` is

```ruby
where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host).first
```

which compares against a bare hostname such as `eviltrout.com`.

### Theory / Proof

The old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` (removed in this PR) explicitly accepted `http://eviltrout.com` and `https://eviltrout.com` -- the deleted specs `works with a http host` / `works with a https host` covered exactly that, and the PR's own controller spec still uses `https://example.com/1234`. The normalisation that makes those work now lives only in the model's `before_validation` hook (strip scheme, strip path), which raw SQL in a migration bypasses. So a stored value of `http://eviltrout.com` becomes a row whose `host` is `http://eviltrout.com`, and `lower('http://eviltrout.com') = 'eviltrout.com'` is false.

Also:
- `split("\n")` leaves a trailing `\r` on CRLF input and yields empty strings for blank lines, both of which become unmatchable rows.
- `'#{h}'` is unescaped; a value containing `'` breaks the migration.

### What happens today vs. what will break

Before upgrade, `http://eviltrout.com` in the setting allowed referers from `eviltrout.com`. After the migration, `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` raises `InvalidAccess('invalid referer host')` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` returns true, so embedded comments stop loading with no admin-visible error; the setting that held the value is also deleted.

### Research

Rails guidance for data migrations is to either use the model (with a local model class) or replicate its normalisation; `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote` is the standard escape for interpolated values.

### Recommendation

```ruby
val.split(/\r?\n/).map(&:strip).reject(&:blank?).each do |h|
  h = h.sub(/^https?:\/\//, '').sub(/\/.*$/, '')
  next if h.blank?
  execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at)
           VALUES (#{ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)}, #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"
end
```
kept.evidence: The raw INSERT at lines 22-25 bypasses the before_validation hook (embeddable_host.rb:5-8). The old allows_embeddable_host? accepted http:// and https:// prefixes and had specs covering them. record_for_host (embeddable_host.rb:17) compares against a bare uri.host, so migrated prefixed rows never match. The old setting is deleted at line 31. The unquoted '#{h}' breaks the migration on values containing a quote. The CRLF and blank-line cases are unlikely through the value-list UI.

kept.claim: record_for_host lowercases the stored column but not the incoming host. An embed_url whose hostname contains uppercase letters (passed unchanged from discourseEmbedUrl to TopicRetriever and TopicEmbed.import) is therefore rejected, or gets no category, even though the host is registered.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Case-insensitive match is only half applied: the incoming host is not downcased

**Severity:** LOW -- embed URLs with uppercase characters in the hostname are not retrieved, and their topics get no host category.

### The Problem

```ruby
host = uri.host
return false unless host.present?

where("lower(host) = ?", host).first
```

`lower()` on the column shows the intent is a case-insensitive match, but the bound parameter is used as-is.

### Theory / Proof

Ruby's `URI::Generic#host` returns the host exactly as written; only `#normalize` downcases it. RFC 3986 section 3.2.2 says the host is case-insensitive. The `embed_url` comes from the blog's `discourseEmbedUrl` (public/javascripts/embed.js), and `EmbedController` passes it unchanged into `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` -> `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(@embed_url)`. If the hostname is `Blog.Example.com`, the SQL is `'blog.example.com' = 'Blog.Example.com'`, which is false, so the topic is never retrieved. `TopicEmbed.import` also calls `record_for_host(url)` and gets no category.

### What happens today vs. what will break

The referer check in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` is not affected in practice, because browsers send a lowercased host in `Referer`. The failure is limited to the `embed_url` paths. The old `allows_embeddable_host?` was case-sensitive as well, so this is not a regression. It is an incomplete implementation of the case-insensitive match the new code clearly intends.

### Recommendation

```ruby
where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase).first
```

(or downcase in `before_validation` and compare `host = ?` directly).
kept.evidence: embeddable_host.rb:14-17 lowercases only the column; URI#host keeps the input's case. An embed_url is passed unchanged from embed.js:14 through embed_controller.rb to topic_retriever.rb:15-16, so retrieval is skipped and TopicEmbed.import gets no category. The referer check is not affected in practice because browsers lowercase the Referer host. The old code was also case-sensitive, so this is not a regression.
kept.corrected_claim: record_for_host lowercases the stored column but not the incoming host. An embed_url whose hostname contains uppercase letters (passed unchanged from discourseEmbedUrl to TopicRetriever and TopicEmbed.import) is therefore rejected, or gets no category, even though the host is registered.

kept.claim: Replacing SiteSetting.embed_category with the per-host category means TopicEmbed.import calls from Jobs::PollFeed for feed items whose host is not a registered EmbeddableHost now create Uncategorized topics. Previously they went to the configured embed category, and the PR removes any way to configure a default.
kept.body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] Feed-polled topics lose their category when the item host is not an EmbeddableHost

**Severity:** MEDIUM -- behavioural regression for sites using `feed_polling_enabled`; imported topics silently land in Uncategorized.

### The Problem

```ruby
eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)

creator = PostCreator.new(user,
                          ...
                          category: eh.try(:category_id))
```

`TopicEmbed.import` is not only reached through `TopicRetriever` (which first checks `host_allowed?`). `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:39` calls it directly for every item in `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url`, with no host check. Feed item URLs can be on a host that is not in `embeddable_hosts` (feedburner/proxy links, a different subdomain, or simply a feed-only setup with no comment embedding).

### Theory / Proof

When `record_for_host` returns `false`/`nil`, `eh.try(:category_id)` is `nil`, and `TopicCreator#find_category` (lib/topic_creator.rb:110-120) then finds no category, so `topic_params[:category_id]` is never set and `Topic` falls back to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` (app/models/topic.rb:216-217). Before this PR, `SiteSetting.embed_category` applied to every imported topic regardless of host. The PR deletes `embed_category` entirely (site_settings.yml and the migration's `DELETE FROM site_settings`), so there is no longer any way to configure a category for such topics.

### What happens today vs. what will break

If every feed URL host is registered, behaviour is unchanged. A site that polls `https://feeds.example.com/...` whose items link to `https://www.example.com/...` while only `example.com` is registered -- or that uses feed polling without registering hosts -- now gets uncategorized topics after upgrade.

### Recommendation

Keep a configurable fallback. For example, keep `embed_category` as a site-wide default and use it when no host matches:

```ruby
eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)
category = eh.try(:category_id) || SiteSetting.embed_category.presence
```

(Falling back to `uncategorized_category_id` would change nothing, because `Topic` already applies that default.) If a site-wide default is not wanted, at least document that feed-polled URLs must be on registered hosts.
kept.evidence: poll_feed.rb:37-40 calls TopicEmbed.import with no host check. topic_embed.rb:36-43 now uses eh.try(:category_id), which is nil for hosts that are not registered. topic_creator.rb:110-120 then sets no category, and topic.rb:216-217 defaults the topic to Uncategorized. The embed_category setting is deleted, so there is no configurable fallback. Caveat: the topic lands in Uncategorized rather than having no category, and a fallback to uncategorized_category_id would change nothing.

kept.claim: The host format regex rejects valid hostnames that the old free-text setting accepted -- TLDs longer than 5 characters (e.g. .community, .technology), 'localhost', single-label intranet hosts and IP addresses -- and it accepts host:port values that record_for_host can never match because it compares against URI#host (no port).
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Host validation regex rejects valid hosts and accepts unmatchable `host:port` entries

**Severity:** MEDIUM -- admins cannot register legitimate embedding hosts, and some accepted entries never match.

### The Problem

```ruby
validates_format_of :host, :with => /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i
```

- `\.[a-z]{2,5}` caps the TLD at 5 letters. `example.community`, `blog.technology`, `foo.software`, `bar.museum` (6) all fail validation.
- A dot and alphabetic TLD are mandatory, so `localhost`, `intranet`, and IPs such as `192.168.1.10` are rejected -- these are common in staging setups.
- `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` accepts `example.com:8080`, but `record_for_host` looks up `uri.host`, which never contains the port, so such a row can never match any referer.

### Theory / Proof

IANA's root zone has contained hundreds of TLDs longer than 5 characters since the 2013-2014 gTLD expansion (e.g. `.photography`, `.community`). RFC 1123 section 2.1 allows single-label hostnames and dotted-quad IPs. The previous implementation (`SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?`) had no format validation at all, so any of these worked before this PR. `URI::Generic#host` excludes the port (it is in `#port`), so `lower(host) = 'example.com'` vs stored `example.com:8080` never matches.

### What happens today vs. what will break

The admin UI shows a validation error when adding such a host and there is no way around it. Rows migrated from the old setting bypass validation, but editing them later in the new UI will fail validation.

### Recommendation

Validate by parsing rather than regex, and drop ports (or store and compare them explicitly):

```ruby
validate :host_must_be_valid

def host_must_be_valid
  uri = URI.parse("http://#{host}") rescue nil
  errors.add(:host, :invalid) unless uri && uri.host.present? && uri.port == 80
end
```

or at minimum widen the TLD part to `[a-z]{2,63}` and remove the port group.
kept.evidence: The regex on embeddable_host.rb:2 caps TLDs at 5 letters, requires a dot and an alphabetic TLD (so localhost and IP addresses are rejected), and accepts :port. record_for_host compares against URI#host, which has no port, so port entries can never match. The old setting had no format validation. Migrated rows bypass validation and will fail it when edited in the new UI.

kept.claim: update and destroy use where(id:).first and then call methods on the result without a nil check, so a request for a non-existent or already-deleted id raises NoMethodError (500) instead of returning 404.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Missing record in update/destroy raises NoMethodError (500) instead of 404

**Severity:** LOW -- admin-only, but produces 500s and error-log noise on double-delete or stale UI.

### The Problem

```ruby
def destroy
  host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first
  host.destroy
  ...
end

def update
  host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first
  save_host(host)   # save_host calls host.host = ...
end
```

`.first` returns `nil` when the id does not exist, then `nil.destroy` / `nil.host=` raises `NoMethodError`.

### Theory / Proof

Two admins with the page open, or one admin double-clicking delete, is enough: the second request hits a deleted id. Discourse's `ApplicationController` rescues `Discourse::NotFound` into a 404 JSON response, but `NoMethodError` becomes a 500 and is logged as an exception.

### Research

Sibling admin controllers (e.g. `Admin::PermalinksController#destroy`, `Admin::UserFieldsController`) use `find` / `find_by` with `raise Discourse::NotFound`, or `params.require` + `find`, which yields a clean 404.

### Recommendation

```ruby
def update
  save_host(EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id]))
end

def destroy
  EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id]).destroy
  render json: success_json
end
```

(`ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` is mapped to 404 by Rails/Discourse.)
kept.evidence: embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:10 and :15 call where(...).first and never check for nil; line 16 (destroy) and line 23 (save_host) then call methods on the result. ApplicationController's rescue_from list (application_controller.rb:73-116) does not cover NoMethodError, so a stale or doubled request returns a 500.

kept.claim: before_validation calls sub! on self.host without a nil guard, so saving a record with a nil host (e.g. a PUT/POST without the host param) raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] `before_validation` crashes on nil host instead of producing a validation error

**Severity:** LOW -- turns a bad request into a 500 rather than a 422 with a message.

### The Problem

```ruby
before_validation do
  self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')
  self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')
end
```

`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, which is `nil` if the key is absent. `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?` also reaches this hook with `host == nil`.

### Theory / Proof

`nil.sub!` raises `NoMethodError`. Because the hook runs before `validates_format_of`, the model never gets the chance to add a normal `errors[:host]` entry, so `render_json_error(host)` in the controller is never reached; the client gets a 500 instead of the usual error popup.

The client-side `cantSave` guard only covers the Ember UI; API clients and malformed requests are not protected.

### Recommendation

```ruby
before_validation do
  if host.present?
    self.host = host.strip.sub(/^https?:\/\//, '').sub(/\/.*$/, '')
  end
end

validates :host, presence: true
```

(Using non-bang `sub` with reassignment also avoids mutating the caller's params string in place.)
kept.evidence: embeddable_host.rb:6-7 calls sub! on host without a nil guard. The hook runs before validates_format_of, so a nil host raises NoMethodError, and the render_json_error 422 path in the controller (line 30) is never reached.
